q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Wagons under and awaiting repair are excluded from the effective wagon fleet of a railway.
2. Indices such as Net Tonne Kilometres per wagon day measure the utilisation of wagons.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Wagons under or awaiting repair are ineffective and excluded from the effective fleet; NTKM per wagon day is a standard operating index of wagon utilisation, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The fares collected by IRCTC for e-tickets are the earnings of IRCTC and are not settled with the Railways.
2. The fare amounts on e-tickets are accounted as goods earnings of the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: E-ticket fares collected by IRCTC are settled with and accounted by the Railways as coaching (passenger) earnings, not IRCTC earnings and not goods earnings, so neither statement is correct.

q: Wharfage and demurrage charges have accrued at a station during a month but remain uncollected at the end of the month. The correct treatment in the station accounts is that they are:

options.A: Brought to account on accrual and shown as outstanding till realised
options.B: Ignored till they are actually collected in cash
options.C: Accounted for only in the annual accounts of the railway
options.D: Written off as bad debts at the close of the month

e: Under accrual accounting in station accounts, accrued wharfage and demurrage are brought to account when they accrue and shown as station outstandings until realised.

q: For preparing its periodical statistical statements, a zonal railway draws its basic data mainly from:

options.A: Reports published in newspapers and trade journals
options.B: The returns and statements rendered by the stations and operating units
options.C: The Budget documents issued by the Railway Board
options.D: The inspection reports of the statutory audit department

e: Periodical statistics are compiled from the basic returns and statements rendered by stations and operating units, which are the primary source data of the railway.

q: The flexi fare system, under which the fare is dynamically linked to occupancy, was introduced in:

options.A: All Mail and Express trains
options.B: Suburban train services
options.C: Rajdhani, Shatabdi and Duronto trains
options.D: Passenger (slow local) trains only

e: Flexi fare, with fares varying with occupancy/demand, was introduced in Rajdhani, Shatabdi and Duronto trains, not in all mail/express, suburban or passenger trains.

q: Station-to-Station (STS) rates in goods traffic are:

options.A: Rates applicable uniformly at all stations of the Railways
options.B: Fares applicable to suburban passenger services
options.C: Rates applicable to parcel traffic only
options.D: Concessional freight rates notified for traffic between specified pairs of stations

e: Station-to-Station (STS) rates are special concessional freight rates notified for traffic between specified pairs of stations, departing from the normal class rates.

q: Long Term Tariff Contracts (LTTC) for freight traffic are entered into by the Railways with:

options.A: Key freight customers who assure a minimum volume of traffic over the contract period
options.B: Catering contractors at stations
options.C: Parcel handling contractors at goods sheds
options.D: State Governments for the running of suburban services

e: Long Term Tariff Contracts are freight contracts with key customers who assure a minimum guaranteed volume/revenue of traffic over the contract period in return for agreed terms.

q: A zonal railway invites new and innovative ideas from its staff and the public for earning revenue from non-fare sources, outside the traditional fare and freight earnings. The scheme under which such non-fare revenue initiatives are promoted is:

options.A: Computerisation of station accounts
options.B: Generation of non-fare revenue through new and innovative ideas
options.C: Investment in wagons by freight customers
options.D: Fixation of freight rates for a long period

e: Non-fare revenue is promoted by inviting new and innovative ideas from staff and the public for earnings beyond fare and freight, under the non-fare revenue initiative.

q: A freight terminal developed by a private party for handling rail freight under the freight marketing policy of Indian Railways is abbreviated as PFT, which stands for:

options.A: Public Freight Transport
options.B: Parcel Freight Train
options.C: Private Freight Terminal
options.D: Permanent Freight Terminal

e: PFT stands for Private Freight Terminal, a freight terminal developed by a private party under the freight marketing policy for handling rail freight.

q: The computerised system through which the work of the Traffic Accounts Offices is managed is abbreviated as TAMS, which stands for:

options.A: Train Accounts Management System
options.B: Traffic Audit and Monitoring System
options.C: Terminal Accounts Management System
options.D: Traffic Accounts Management System

e: TAMS stands for Traffic Accounts Management System, the computerised system through which the work of Traffic Accounts Offices is managed.

q: The information system that supports coaching operations, as distinct from the Freight Operations Information System for goods operations, is abbreviated as COIS, which stands for:

options.A: Coaching Operations Information System
options.B: Coaching Outward Information System
options.C: Central Operations and Information Section
options.D: Coaching Operations Inspection Service

e: COIS stands for Coaching Operations Information System, the information system supporting coaching operations, as distinct from FOIS for freight operations.

q: Reservations all over Indian Railways are made through the Passenger Reservation System (PRS), which runs on the computer software known as:

options.A: UTS
options.B: CONCERT
options.C: FOIS
options.D: TAMS

e: The Passenger Reservation System (PRS) runs on CONCERT software; UTS is for unreserved ticketing, FOIS for freight and TAMS for traffic accounts.

q: The Passenger Reservation System and the Freight Operations Information System used all over Indian Railways were developed, and are maintained, by:

options.A: Rail India Technical and Economic Service (RITES)
options.B: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC)
options.C: Centre for Railway Information Systems (CRIS)
options.D: RailTel Corporation of India

e: PRS and FOIS were developed and are maintained by CRIS, the Centre for Railway Information Systems, the Railways' information technology organisation.

q: A passenger uses the enquiry system of Indian Railways to find out the running position of a train. This system is abbreviated as NTES, which stands for:

options.A: National Ticket Enquiry Service
options.B: National Train Earnings Statement
options.C: Network of Ticket Examining Staff
options.D: National Train Enquiry System

e: NTES stands for National Train Enquiry System, the system through which passengers enquire about train running position and related information.

q: Under a liberalised scheme of Indian Railways, freight customers could invest in wagons of their own, which were operated by the Railways for their traffic. This scheme is abbreviated as LWIS, which stands for:

options.A: Liberalised Wagon Investment Scheme
options.B: Long-distance Wagon Information System
options.C: Liberalised Wagon Insurance Scheme
options.D: Local Wagon Investment Scheme

e: LWIS stands for Liberalised Wagon Investment Scheme, under which freight customers invest in their own wagons which the Railways operate for their traffic.

q: A passenger is allotted a unique ten-digit reference number at the time of booking a reserved ticket, against which the status of the booking can be enquired. In railway reservation, the abbreviation PNR stands for:

options.A: Passenger Number Reference
options.B: Provisional Name Register
options.C: Passenger Notification Record
options.D: Passenger Name Record

e: PNR stands for Passenger Name Record, the unique ten-digit reference generated at booking against which reservation status can be enquired.

q: At a busy station, passengers obtain unreserved tickets from self-service machines installed in the circulating area instead of standing in the booking-office queue. In connection with unreserved ticketing, the abbreviation ATVM stands for:

options.A: Automatic Ticket Vending Machine
options.B: All-India Ticket Verification Module
options.C: Assisted Ticket Vending Machine
options.D: Automatic Train Vacancy Monitor

e: ATVM stands for Automatic Ticket Vending Machine, the self-service machine from which passengers obtain unreserved tickets at stations.

q: A passenger holding a Reservation Against Cancellation ticket boards the train without a confirmed berth. As distinguished from a waitlisted passenger, he is entitled to:

options.A: A confirmed berth in the next higher class
options.B: Sitting accommodation in the reserved coach, with a berth allotted as and when a vacancy arises on cancellation
options.C: A full refund of fare at the destination station
options.D: Travel by any other train on the same day without further charge

e: A Reservation Against Cancellation (RAC) passenger may board and occupy sitting accommodation in the reserved coach, getting a berth as and when a vacancy arises on cancellation.

q: The Railways cancel a train fully for operational reasons and a passenger holding a confirmed ticket for that train claims a refund. The correct position is that he is entitled to:

options.A: Refund of fare after deduction of the prescribed cancellation charge
options.B: Refund of only fifty per cent of the fare
options.C: Full refund of fare without deduction of any cancellation charge
options.D: No refund, but free rebooking on any future date

e: Where the Railways cancel a train fully, a confirmed ticket holder gets a full refund of fare without deduction of cancellation charges, as the failure is the Railways'.

q: A passenger is accommodated in a lower class although he holds a reserved ticket for a higher class, and the ticket checking staff issue him a certificate for the change. On the basis of that certificate, he is entitled to claim:

options.A: No refund of any kind
options.B: Refund of the full fare of the higher class
options.C: A berth in the higher class in the next train
options.D: Refund of the difference of fare between the class booked and the class actually travelled in

e: On travelling in a lower class than booked, certified by the checking staff, the passenger can claim refund of the difference between the fare of the class booked and the class travelled.

q: A passenger presents luggage weighing more than the free allowance admissible to him for his class of travel. The excess luggage:

options.A: Must be booked and is charged at the prescribed luggage rates
options.B: Is carried free up to twice the free allowance
options.C: Is charged at the goods freight rates in all cases
options.D: Must be refused carriage at the station

e: Luggage beyond the free allowance for the class must be booked and charged at the prescribed luggage rates; it is not carried free or automatically at goods rates.

q: A consignor disputes the weight on which freight has been charged, contending that only the actual weight of his consignment can be taken. In goods booking, the 'chargeable weight' of a consignment means:

options.A: The weight as declared by the consignor, in all cases
options.B: The actual weight of the consignment or the minimum weight condition prescribed for the wagon or class of traffic, whichever is higher
options.C: The carrying capacity of the wagon used, in all cases
options.D: The average weight of similar consignments booked at the station

e: Chargeable weight is the actual weight or the minimum weight condition prescribed for the wagon/class of traffic, whichever is higher, as per goods tariff rules.

q:
A goods clerk traces how the invoice of a consignment moves between the booking station and the destination station. Consider the following statements in this regard:
1. The forwarding station prepares the goods invoice in copies, one copy travelling with the consignment to its destination.
2. On delivery, the destination station checks the consignment against the invoice particulars and builds up its inward returns from the invoices so received.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The forwarding station prepares the goods invoice in copies, one travelling with the consignment, and the destination builds its inward returns after checking delivery against those invoices.

q: Two zonal railways of different route lengths are compared for the earnings generated per unit of line open for traffic. 'Earnings per route kilometre' of a railway is computed as:

options.A: Goods earnings divided by goods train kilometres
options.B: Net revenue divided by the capital-at-charge
options.C: Passenger earnings divided by passenger kilometres
options.D: Gross traffic earnings divided by the route kilometres open for traffic

e: Earnings per route kilometre is gross traffic earnings divided by the route kilometres open for traffic, a standard financial/statistical ratio.

q: For passenger statistics, a zonal railway counts not only the passengers who began their journey at its own stations but also those handed over to it by neighbouring railways. 'Passengers carried' on a railway comprise:

options.A: Originating passengers plus the passengers received from other railways
options.B: Only the passengers who alight at its stations
options.C: Only the passengers booked at its own stations against cash payment
options.D: The passengers who travel by reserved coaches only

e: Passengers carried comprise originating passengers plus passengers received from other railways; counting only originating passengers would understate traffic actually carried.

q: At the destination station, an undercharge is detected on a 'to-pay' consignment before the goods are handed over to the consignee. The undercharge is:

options.A: Written off by the destination station
options.B: Recovered from the consignee before delivery of the goods
options.C: Recovered from the staff of the forwarding station
options.D: Adjusted against the sundry earnings of the station

e: An undercharge detected on a to-pay consignment at destination is recovered from the consignee before delivery, as freight dues must be collected before the goods are handed over.

q: A passenger travelling by a superfast train pays, besides the ordinary fare, a superfast charge. In the earnings accounts, this superfast charge forms part of:

options.A: Sundry other earnings
options.B: Goods earnings
options.C: Coaching earnings
options.D: Miscellaneous receipts of the division

e: The superfast charge levied on superfast trains is part of coaching earnings, being a charge on passenger travel, not sundry, goods or miscellaneous receipts.

q: A consignee is able to transfer his right to take delivery of a consignment to another person merely by endorsing and handing over a document. A Railway Receipt is a document of title to the goods, which means that:

options.A: It can never be transferred to another person
options.B: It is valid only in favour of the consignor named on it
options.C: It serves only as a cash receipt for the freight paid
options.D: The right to take delivery of the goods can be transferred by endorsement and delivery of the Railway Receipt

e: A Railway Receipt is a document of title: the right to take delivery can be transferred by endorsement and delivery of the receipt to the endorsee.

q: The widow of a passenger who died in an untoward incident seeks compensation for the death. Claims for compensation for death of, or injury to, passengers in a train accident or an untoward incident are decided by the:

options.A: Railway Claims Tribunal
options.B: Divisional Railway Manager
options.C: Railway Board
options.D: District Consumer Commission only

e: Claims for compensation for death or injury in a train accident or untoward incident are decided by the Railway Claims Tribunal under the Railway Claims Tribunal Act, 1987.

q: A person found travelling without a proper ticket argues before the ticket checking staff that the excess charge demanded from him is itself the fare for his journey. The correct position is that the excess charge leviable under the Railways Act is payable:

options.A: In lieu of the ordinary fare for the distance travelled
options.B: In addition to the ordinary fare due for the distance travelled
options.C: Only where the person is also found carrying excess luggage
options.D: Only by season ticket holders found in reserved coaches

e: Under the Railways Act, the excess charge for ticketless or irregular travel is payable in addition to the ordinary fare due for the distance travelled, not in lieu of it.

q: A party seeks waiver of demurrage accrued at a station on the ground that the wagons were placed before him in a bunch, in excess of his requirements, so that he could not unload them all within the free time allowed. Which of the following is a recognised circumstance in which waiver of demurrage may be considered by the competent authority?

options.A: The consignee is a regular customer of the Railways
options.B: The goods carried in the wagons are of high value
options.C: Wagons were placed in a bunch, in excess of the party's requirements, so that unloading within the free time was not practicable
options.D: The station at which the demurrage accrued is a busy terminal station

e: Bunch placement of wagons in excess of the party's requirements, making unloading within free time impracticable, is a recognised ground for considering waiver of demurrage.

q: A passenger who has booked a confirmed Tatkal ticket himself cancels it before the journey and demands a refund of the fare. The correct position is that:

options.A: Full fare is refunded without any deduction
options.B: Fifty per cent of the fare is refunded
options.C: Only the reservation charge is refunded
options.D: No refund is admissible, except in the circumstances specified in the refund rules such as cancellation of the train

e: No refund is admissible on a confirmed Tatkal ticket cancelled by the passenger, except in specified circumstances in the refund rules such as cancellation of the train.

q: Coal is loaded in bulk in an open wagon for carriage as goods traffic. Freight on such bulk commodities loaded in open wagons is generally charged on the basis of:

options.A: The carrying capacity of the wagon used
options.B: The volume of the wagon
options.C: A flat rate per wagon, irrespective of the wagon used
options.D: The market value of the commodity

e: For bulk commodities in open wagons, freight is generally charged on the carrying capacity of the wagon used, applying the prescribed minimum weight condition.

q: A merchant offers traffic in wagon loads, but the quantity offered does not make up a full rake load. 'Wagonload' class rates in goods traffic are applicable where:

options.A: A full rake load of traffic is offered for booking
options.B: Traffic is offered in wagon loads which do not make up a full rake load
options.C: Traffic is carried in the brake vans of passenger trains
options.D: The consignment weighs less than the prescribed minimum for 'smalls'

e: Wagonload class rates apply where traffic is offered in wagon loads, even if the wagons offered do not make up a full rake (train) load.

q:
The FOIS terminal at a goods station remains down for several hours and booking work has to continue in the meantime. Consider the following statements about this situation:
1. During the failure, goods booking is done manually under the prescribed contingency arrangements.
2. Once the system is restored, the particulars of the consignments so booked manually are fed into it, so that the traffic is duly accounted for.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: During FOIS failure, booking continues manually under contingency arrangements, and on restoration the manually booked particulars are fed into FOIS so the traffic is duly accounted.

q: A passenger pays, over and above the ordinary fare, a premium for obtaining confirmed reservation at short notice under the Tatkal scheme. In the earnings accounts, Tatkal premium charges collected from passengers form part of:

options.A: Sundry other earnings
options.B: Passenger (coaching) earnings
options.C: Goods earnings
options.D: Miscellaneous receipts of the division

e: Tatkal premium charges are part of passenger (coaching) earnings, being a premium on the passenger fare for confirmed reservation at short notice.

q: An operating officer works out how fast passenger trains run on his railway over a period, taking the time actually taken by the trains into account. The average speed of passenger trains is computed as:

options.A: Route kilometres divided by the number of trains run
options.B: Passenger kilometres divided by passenger train hours
options.C: Vehicle kilometres divided by vehicle days
options.D: Passenger train kilometres divided by the corresponding train hours

e: Average speed of passenger trains is passenger train kilometres divided by the corresponding passenger train hours, i.e. distance run per hour actually taken.

q: As distinguished from indices of wagon utilisation in goods working, 'passenger kilometres per vehicle day' is an index which measures:

options.A: The traffic output obtained from coaching vehicles, that is, their utilisation in terms of passenger traffic performed
options.B: The speed of coaching services
options.C: The earnings of coaching services per day
options.D: The punctuality of passenger trains

e: Passenger kilometres per vehicle day measures traffic output per coaching vehicle per day, i.e. utilisation of coaching vehicles in passenger traffic performed.

q:
At the close of the financial year, a zonal railway has delivered certain goods on which the 'to-pay' freight is still unpaid. Consider the following statements about the treatment of this amount:
1. Because railway earnings are accounted on the accrual basis, the unpaid freight is included in the earnings of that year itself.
2. Till it is realised or adjusted, the unpaid amount remains held under Traffic Suspense.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Railway earnings are on accrual basis, so unpaid to-pay freight for goods delivered is included in that year's earnings and held under Traffic Suspense till realised or adjusted.

q: A consignee asks to take his goods away first and to pay the demurrage and wharfage due on the consignment later. The correct position is that demurrage and wharfage charges due on a consignment are required to be paid:

options.A: Within thirty days of delivery of the goods
options.B: Before the goods are delivered or removed from the station premises
options.C: At the end of the financial year in which they accrued
options.D: Only if the amount exceeds the freight paid on the consignment

e: Demurrage and wharfage due on a consignment must be paid before the goods are delivered or removed from station premises; delivery first and payment later is not permitted.

q: A dispute arises about the period for which demurrage is payable at a goods terminal. Demurrage at a goods terminal is computed with reference to:

options.A: The time of placement of the wagons for loading or unloading and the time of their release, as recorded in the terminal records or system
options.B: The date of booking of the consignment
options.C: The date of preparation of the Railway Receipt
options.D: The date of arrival of the train at the nearest junction

e: Demurrage is computed from the time of placement of wagons for loading/unloading to the time of their release, as recorded in terminal records or the system.

q: A consignee receiving a consignment at the destination station doubts the weight recorded against it and wants the consignment weighed again in his presence. He may obtain its re-weighment at the destination station:

options.A: Free of charge in all cases
options.B: Only through an order of the Railway Claims Tribunal
options.C: Only at the forwarding station from which it was booked
options.D: On payment of the prescribed weighment charges

e: Re-weighment of a consignment at destination can be obtained on payment of the prescribed weighment charges; it is not free in all cases or confined to the forwarding station.

q: As distinguished from goods traffic, which moves in goods trains, parcel traffic on Indian Railways is generally carried:

options.A: Only by goods trains
options.B: Only by road vehicles hired by the Railways
options.C: By passenger-carrying trains, in brake or luggage vans and parcel vans attached to them
options.D: Only by special parcel trains and by no other train

e: Parcel traffic is generally carried by passenger-carrying trains in brake/luggage vans and parcel vans attached to them, unlike goods traffic moving in goods trains.

q: A debit raised against a station on account of an error in its accounts is traced to the negligence of a particular member of the station staff. Amounts so debited to a station on account of errors or deficiencies in its accounts are ultimately:

options.A: Borne by the Railways as a normal loss in all cases
options.B: Recoverable from the members of the station staff found responsible for the error or deficiency
options.C: Adjusted against the sundry earnings of the station
options.D: Recovered from the passengers and merchants concerned

e: Debits raised for errors or deficiencies in station accounts are ultimately recoverable from the station staff member found responsible for the error or deficiency.

q: During internal check, the Traffic Accounts Office examines the Parcel Way Bills rendered by a station. This check is exercised primarily to ensure that:

options.A: The parcels were delivered on the day of their arrival
options.B: The parcel vans were utilised to their full capacity
options.C: The parcels were carried only by Rajdhani trains
options.D: The parcel charges have been correctly levied in accordance with the scales in force and duly brought to account

e: Internal check of Parcel Way Bills in the Traffic Accounts Office ensures parcel charges were correctly levied under the scales in force and duly brought to account.

q: A station submits bills for amounts claimed by contractors engaged for loading and unloading work at the goods shed. 'Handling bills' rendered by stations relate to:

options.A: Payments claimed by contractors engaged for handling, loading and unloading of goods and parcels at stations
options.B: Bills for the pay and allowances of goods shed staff
options.C: Bills for the printing of goods invoices
options.D: Claims of merchants for goods damaged in transit

e: Handling bills are claims of contractors engaged for handling, loading and unloading of goods and parcels at stations, rendered by the stations for payment.

q: After apportionment, the total traffic earnings of Indian Railways as a whole are found to be exactly what they were before apportionment. This is because the apportionment of earnings of through traffic among the zonal railways has the effect of:

options.A: Increasing the total earnings of Indian Railways
options.B: Merely distributing the through earnings among the railways concerned, without altering the total earnings of Indian Railways as a whole
options.C: Reducing the total earnings of Indian Railways
options.D: Transferring the entire earnings to the Railway Board

e: Apportionment only distributes through-traffic earnings among the railways concerned according to their shares; the total earnings of Indian Railways as a whole remain unchanged.

q: A station master is asked by a merchant whether he can revise the freight rate for a commodity at his station. Passenger fares and freight rates on Indian Railways are fixed by:

options.A: The Station Master at each station
options.B: The Finance Commission
options.C: The Railway Board (Ministry of Railways)
options.D: The respective State Governments

e: Passenger fares and freight rates on Indian Railways are fixed by the Railway Board (Ministry of Railways), not by station masters, State Governments or the Finance Commission.

q: Small consignments which do not make up a wagon load cost more to handle per unit of weight than wagonload traffic. 'Smalls' traffic is therefore charged for carriage:

options.A: At trainload rates
options.B: At parcel rates in all cases
options.C: Free of charge up to the prescribed minimum weight
options.D: At a scale of rates which is higher per unit of weight than the wagonload scale, in view of the higher cost of handling such traffic

e: Smalls, being costlier to handle per unit weight, are charged at a scale higher per unit of weight than the wagonload scale, as provided in the goods tariff.

q: For the same commodity and the same distance, the rate charged per tonne when a full rake load is offered is compared with the rate for a wagon load. Trainload (rake-load) class rates, as compared with wagonload class rates, are generally:

options.A: Lower per tonne, in view of the economies of full-rake movement
options.B: Higher per tonne
options.C: Exactly equal per tonne
options.D: Applicable only to trains carrying passengers

e: Trainload (rake-load) class rates are generally lower per tonne than wagonload rates, reflecting the economies of moving traffic in full rakes.

q: Heavy consignments at a station are loaded into wagons with the help of a railway crane, and the merchant is asked to pay crane charges over and above the freight. The correct position is that such crane charges are:

options.A: Borne by the Railways in all cases
options.B: Recovered from the consignor or the consignee, as the case may be, in addition to the freight
options.C: Adjusted against the demurrage accrued on the consignment
options.D: Included in the wharfage charges of the station

e: Crane charges for loading or unloading heavy consignments with a railway crane are recovered from the consignor or consignee, as applicable, in addition to the freight.

q: An accounts clerk has to look up the rules dealing with traffic earnings, station accounts and traffic statistics. These accounts are dealt with in:

options.A: Accounts Code, Volume I
options.B: Accounts Code, Volume III
options.C: Accounts Code, Volume II
options.D: Accounts Code, Volume IV

e: Traffic earnings, station accounts and traffic statistics are dealt with in the Indian Railways Code for the Accounts Department, i.e. Accounts Code Volume II.

q: In the Traffic Accounts Office, the outward returns of forwarding stations are tallied with the inward returns of destination stations. This tally is carried out primarily to ensure that:

options.A: Wagons are allotted equitably among stations
options.B: The tariffs in use at stations are printed correctly
options.C: The staff posted at stations are correctly shown
options.D: All traffic booked is duly accounted for and no consignment or freight escapes accountal

e: Tallying outward returns of forwarding stations with inward returns of destination stations ensures all traffic booked is duly accounted and no consignment or freight escapes accountal.

q: As distinguished from station outstandings, 'Cash-in-Transit' in traffic accounts represents:

options.A: Station earnings collected but not yet credited to the Railway's account, being in the process of remittance
options.B: The cash held in the station imprest
options.C: Cash paid out as refunds to passengers
options.D: Uncollected 'to-pay' freight outstanding at the station

e: Cash-in-Transit is station earnings collected but not yet credited to the Railways' account, being in the process of remittance to the bank or cash office.

q:
An auditor asks what kinds of amounts are held under Traffic Suspense on a zonal railway. Consider the following statements in reply:
1. The pay and allowances due to the station staff are held under Traffic Suspense.
2. Charges for traffic booked on credit notes or warrants for Government departments, awaiting recovery from those departments, are held under Traffic Suspense.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Traffic Suspense holds traffic dues awaiting recovery, such as charges on credit notes and warrants for Government departments; pay and allowances of staff are not held under it, so only statement 2 is correct.

q:
A parcel clerk is asked whether the same parcel charges apply whatever the train by which a parcel is carried. Consider the following statements in this connection:
1. One uniform scale of parcel charges applies to parcels carried by every type of train.
2. Parcel charges are levied under different scales according to the type of train, namely the Rajdhani scale (R), the Premium scale (P) and the Standard scale (S).
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Parcel charges are levied under different scales by train type - Rajdhani (R), Premium (P) and Standard (S) - so there is no single uniform scale; only statement 2 is correct.

q: Charges are realised at a station for the carriage of dogs and horses by passenger trains. In the earnings accounts, such charges are classified under:

options.A: Goods earnings
options.B: Sundry other earnings
options.C: Passenger fares
options.D: Other Coaching Earnings

e: Charges for carriage of dogs, horses and other animals by passenger trains are classified as Other Coaching Earnings, not goods earnings, passenger fares or sundry earnings.

q: A merchant is granted a refund of freight on goods traffic found to have been overcharged. In the railway accounts, refunds of freight granted to merchants on goods traffic are accounted for:

options.A: By deduction from the goods earnings
options.B: As expenditure of the Commercial Department
options.C: Through the salary bills of the goods shed staff
options.D: Only at the close of the financial year

e: Refunds of freight overcharged on goods traffic are accounted for by deduction from goods earnings, reversing the excess originally brought to account as earnings.

q: The annual earnings budget of a railway is spread over the twelve months of the year for comparison with the actual earnings of each month. The budget proportions so fixed for the months:

options.A: Are a uniform one-twelfth of the annual earnings budget for every month
options.B: Are fixed only for the first six months of the year
options.C: Take into account the seasonal pattern of traffic over the months of the year
options.D: Are fixed by each station for its own earnings separately

e: Monthly budget proportions of annual earnings are fixed taking into account the seasonal pattern of traffic over the year, not as a uniform one-twelfth for every month.

q: A zonal railway has a large number of old items outstanding under Traffic Suspense and a drive is launched for their clearance. The outstandings under Traffic Suspense are, for this purpose:

options.A: Written off in full at the end of every quarter
options.B: Reviewed only at the time of the statutory audit of the railway
options.C: Transferred to the Railway Board for clearance at its level
options.D: Reviewed periodically, item-wise and age-wise, and their clearance pursued with the stations and departments concerned

e: Traffic Suspense outstandings are reviewed periodically item-wise and age-wise, and clearance is pursued with the stations and departments concerned; they are not routinely written off.

q: The tickets sold and the earnings collected at a City Booking Office and at an Out Agency are brought under check in traffic accounts in the manner that:

options.A: Their accounts are rendered to the Traffic Accounts Office and checked there on the lines of station accounts
options.B: Their accounts are checked only by the statutory audit party and by no one else
options.C: No account of their transactions is required to be rendered to the Railways at all
options.D: Their accounts are checked only by the Commercial Department of the division

e: City Booking Offices and Out Agencies render their accounts to the Traffic Accounts Office, where they are checked on the same lines as station accounts.

q:
Consider the following statements about Railway Receipt forms at a station:
1. Railway Receipt forms are unnumbered forms which require no accountal at stations.
2. The used foils of Railway Receipts are destroyed at the station without any check.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Railway Receipt forms are numbered, accountable forms with strict accountal at stations, and used foils are subject to check; both statements denying this are false.

q: A goods clerk has to apply the class shown against a commodity in the goods tariff. The classification of commodities for the purpose of goods freight rating is issued by:

options.A: The Centre for Railway Information Systems
options.B: The Railway Rates Tribunal
options.C: The Indian Railway Conference Association (IRCA)
options.D: The Accounts Directorate of the Railway Board

e: Classification of commodities for goods freight rating is issued by the Indian Railway Conference Association (IRCA) in the Goods Tariff classification.

q:
Consider the following statements about remission of demurrage:
1. A general remission of demurrage for a station or area can be granted by the goods clerk on his own authority.
2. In exceptional circumstances, such as floods or strikes, demurrage may be remitted generally for a station or area under the orders of the competent authority.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: A goods clerk cannot grant general remission on his own; in exceptional circumstances like floods or strikes, general remission may be ordered by the competent authority, so only statement 2 is correct.

q: A claimant is advised to approach the Railway Claims Tribunal for compensation for non-delivery of his consignment. The Railway Claims Tribunal has been set up under:

options.A: The Railways Act, 1989
options.B: The Consumer Protection Act
options.C: The Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996
options.D: The Railway Claims Tribunal Act, 1987

e: The Railway Claims Tribunal was set up under the Railway Claims Tribunal Act, 1987, to decide claims against the railway administration.

q: A passenger cancels a reserved ticket and, besides the fare, also demands back the reservation charge paid by him. On cancellation of a reserved ticket, the reservation charge:

options.A: Is refunded to the passenger in full
options.B: Is refunded to the extent of fifty per cent
options.C: Is not refunded to the passenger
options.D: Is adjusted against the fare of the passenger's next booking

e: On cancellation of a reserved ticket, the reservation charge is not refunded; only the fare is refunded after deducting the prescribed cancellation charges.

q:
Consider the following statements about Suvidha trains:
1. Suvidha trains are premium trains whose fares are dynamic and linked to demand.
2. Waitlisted tickets are issued to passengers in Suvidha trains.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Suvidha trains are premium trains with dynamic, demand-linked fares and only confirmed tickets are issued, with no waitlisted tickets, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: A statistics clerk is told that the operating statistics of his railway are not compiled for the railway as one undivided whole. The operating statistics of Indian Railways are compiled:

options.A: Only for the Broad Gauge system
options.B: Separately for the Broad Gauge, Metre Gauge and Narrow Gauge systems
options.C: For each division separately, but never gauge-wise
options.D: Only once, at the close of the financial year

e: Operating statistics are compiled separately for the Broad Gauge, Metre Gauge and Narrow Gauge systems, as performance and costs differ by gauge.

q: The widow of a passenger killed in an untoward incident is told that she need not prove any negligence of the Railways to get compensation. Under Section 124A of the Railways Act, 1989, compensation for death or injury in an untoward incident is payable by the railway administration:

options.A: Only if negligence of the railway staff is proved
options.B: On the principle of no-fault liability, whether or not there was any wrongful act or negligence on the part of the Railways
options.C: Only if the passenger was travelling on a reserved ticket
options.D: Only after the criminal case against the offender is decided

e: Section 124A of the Railways Act, 1989 imposes no-fault liability: compensation for an untoward incident is payable whether or not there was wrongful act or negligence by the Railways.

q: Which of the following occurrences is included in the definition of an 'untoward incident' under Section 123 of the Railways Act, 1989?

options.A: Detention of a train on account of fog
options.B: Failure of signalling equipment at a station
options.C: Cancellation of a train for operational reasons
options.D: The accidental falling of a passenger from a train carrying passengers

e: Section 123 of the Railways Act, 1989 includes the accidental falling of a passenger from a train carrying passengers in the definition of an untoward incident.

q: A consignor sues the Railways for a consignment lost in transit. Under Section 93 of the Railways Act, 1989, the railway administration is responsible for the loss, destruction, damage or non-delivery of goods entrusted to it:

options.A: As a carrier
options.B: Only as a bailee of the goods
options.C: Only where the goods were booked at railway risk
options.D: Only where the consignor has paid the percentage charge

e: Under Section 93 of the Railways Act, 1989, the railway administration is responsible as a carrier for loss, destruction, damage or non-delivery of goods entrusted to it.

q: A passenger's suitcase, which he had kept with himself in the compartment without booking it, is stolen during the journey. Under Section 100 of the Railways Act, 1989, the position regarding luggage carried by a passenger in his own custody is that the railway administration:

options.A: Is responsible for its loss in the same manner as for booked luggage
options.B: Is not responsible for its loss or damage unless the luggage is booked and a receipt is granted to the passenger
options.C: Is responsible only where the passenger holds a first class ticket
options.D: Is responsible only in case of a train accident

e: Under Section 100, the Railways are not responsible for luggage carried in a passenger's own custody unless it is booked and a receipt is granted for it.

q: A passenger pulls the alarm chain of a running train without any reasonable cause, merely to get down at a place of his choice. Under Section 141 of the Railways Act, 1989, a passenger who needlessly interferes with the means of communication in a train without reasonable and sufficient cause:

options.A: Is liable to pay only the fare for the extra distance travelled
options.B: Is liable to have his season ticket forfeited
options.C: Commits no offence if the train stops and restarts promptly
options.D: Commits an offence punishable under the Act

e: Under Section 141, needlessly interfering with the means of communication in a train, such as alarm chain pulling without reasonable and sufficient cause, is an offence punishable under the Act.

q: A litigant asks who hears his claim before the Railway Claims Tribunal. The Railway Claims Tribunal consists of:

options.A: Only retired railway officers nominated by the Railway Board
options.B: A District Judge and two railway officers of each zonal railway
options.C: A Chairman and such number of Vice-Chairmen and Judicial and Technical Members as may be appointed
options.D: Members elected by the recognised railway unions

e: The Railway Claims Tribunal consists of a Chairman and such number of Vice-Chairmen and Judicial and Technical Members as may be appointed under the 1987 Act.

q: On a zonal railway, a merchant's claim for compensation for goods lost in transit is dealt with, in the first instance, by:

options.A: The Claims organisation of the Commercial Department, headed by the Chief Claims Officer
options.B: The Traffic Accounts Office of the railway
options.C: The Stores Department of the railway
options.D: The Railway Protection Force

e: A merchant's claim for goods lost in transit is dealt with in the first instance by the Claims organisation of the Commercial Department, headed by the Chief Claims Officer.

q: During tally of station accounts it is found that a debit raised on one station really pertains to the traffic transactions of another station. The adjustment between the two stations in such a case is effected through:

options.A: A fresh Railway Receipt issued by the first station
options.B: A Transfer Certificate
options.C: An overcharge sheet
options.D: A cash remittance note

e: A debit pertaining to another station's traffic transactions is adjusted between stations through a Transfer Certificate issued in traffic accounts.

q: At a station, passengers buy tickets from the Automatic Ticket Vending Machines with the help of 'facilitators' standing by the machines. These facilitators are:

options.A: Regular booking clerks of the station working overtime
options.B: Personnel of the Railway Protection Force deputed to the machines
options.C: Agents of IRCTC posted at the station
options.D: Persons engaged for the purpose, who are paid a commission on the tickets sold through them

e: ATVM facilitators are persons engaged for assisting passengers at the machines, paid a commission on the tickets sold through them; they are not regular booking clerks, RPF or IRCTC staff.

q: At a siding terminal, a rake is placed for loading and the locomotive is not detached and sent away while loading goes on. Under the 'Engine-on-Load' arrangement followed at sidings and terminals:

options.A: The locomotive is detached and sent back to the shed as soon as the rake is placed
options.B: The loading of the rake is done by the locomotive crew themselves
options.C: The locomotive remains attached to the rake during loading or unloading, so that detention is reduced and turn-round improves
options.D: Two locomotives are attached to every rake during loading

e: Under Engine-on-Load, the locomotive remains attached to the rake during loading or unloading at sidings/terminals, reducing detention and improving turn-round.

q: As distinguished from the General Purpose Wagon Investment Scheme, under the Special Freight Train Operator (SFTO) scheme of the Railways:

options.A: Private operators invest in special-purpose wagons and rakes for carrying specified bulk commodities
options.B: Private operators are issued free passes for travel in freight trains
options.C: The Railways purchase all the wagons owned by private parties
options.D: Freight rates for all commodities are fixed by the operators themselves

e: Under the Special Freight Train Operator (SFTO) scheme, private operators invest in special-purpose wagons and rakes for specified bulk commodities, unlike general purpose wagons under GPWIS.

q: An end user who does not wish to buy wagons outright wants wagons for his freight movement under the Wagon Leasing Scheme of the Railways. Under this scheme:

options.A: Wagons are leased out by the Railways to passengers for carriage of luggage
options.B: Wagons can be procured on lease from wagon leasing companies by end users and operators for freight movement
options.C: Leasing of wagons is permitted only to the Defence authorities
options.D: Leased wagons cannot be used on the railway network

e: Under the Wagon Leasing Scheme, wagons can be procured on lease from wagon leasing companies by end users and operators for freight movement, without buying them outright.

q: A service provider proposes to run a theme-based tourist circuit train, marketing the tour package himself under the policy of Indian Railways. Such trains are the:

options.A: Bharat Gaurav trains, operated by service providers under the Bharat Gaurav policy
options.B: Freight trains dedicated to the carriage of defence stores
options.C: Suburban trains run in metropolitan cities
options.D: Trains run exclusively for railway employees on duty

e: Theme-based tourist circuit trains marketed by service providers are Bharat Gaurav trains run under the Bharat Gaurav policy of Indian Railways.

q: A freight customer who owes accrued demurrage and other terminal charges at a goods terminal can discharge them without visiting the goods office, namely:

options.A: Only in cash at the goods office of the station
options.B: Only by demand draft sent by post
options.C: Only after the wagons are released from the terminal
options.D: Electronically through the e-payment facility linked with FOIS

e: Accrued demurrage and other terminal charges can be discharged electronically through the e-payment facility linked with FOIS, without visiting the goods office.

q: A freight customer registers his demand for wagons for loading coal at his siding. Registration of demand for wagons (indents) by freight customers can be made:

options.A: Only by appearing in person before the Station Master
options.B: Only through the Travelling Inspector of Accounts
options.C: Electronically through the e-demand facility of the Freight Operations Information System
options.D: Only on the printed forms supplied by the Railway Press

e: Registration of demand for wagons (indents) can be made electronically through the e-demand (e-RD) facility of the Freight Operations Information System.

q: A finance officer closing the earnings abstract of his railway has to keep one of the following receipts out of the gross traffic earnings altogether. Which of the following receipts does NOT form part of the gross traffic earnings of a railway?

options.A: Parcel earnings brought to account for the period
options.B: Demurrage charges realised at stations
options.C: Receipts from advertisements at stations
options.D: Sale proceeds of unserviceable and surplus assets

e: Sale proceeds of unserviceable and surplus assets are capital/miscellaneous receipts, not traffic earnings; parcel earnings and demurrage do form part of gross traffic earnings.

q: At the close of the day, a booking clerk makes an entry of the tickets issued and the coaching earnings of his station for that day. The daily record of the coaching earnings and of the tickets issued at a station is maintained in the:

options.A: Works Register
options.B: Daily Train Cash (DTC) Book
options.C: Contractor's Ledger
options.D: Station Outstanding Register

e: The daily record of tickets issued and coaching earnings at a station is maintained in the Daily Train Cash (DTC) Book.

q: A trader who cannot make up a full rake wants rail carriage for his traffic over a short lead. Under the 'mini rake' facility in goods traffic, freight customers are permitted to:

options.A: Book a full trainload at parcel rates
options.B: Load wagons without placing any indent
options.C: Carry goods free of charge over short distances
options.D: Book a rake smaller than the normal full rake for carriage over short leads, on the conditions prescribed

e: Under the mini rake facility, customers may book a rake smaller than the normal full rake for carriage over short leads, on the prescribed conditions and distance limits.

q: An accounts clerk explains to a probationer what the coaching earnings of his railway consist of. Coaching earnings of a railway comprise:

options.A: Passenger earnings only
options.B: Passenger earnings and other coaching earnings
options.C: Coaching earnings and goods earnings taken together
options.D: Passenger earnings and sundry other earnings taken together

e: Coaching earnings comprise passenger earnings plus other coaching earnings such as parcels, luggage and postal traffic carried by passenger trains.

q: The check exercised by the Traffic Accounts Office over station accounts is described as a 'post-check' because:

options.A: It is exercised after the transactions have taken place and the accounts have been rendered by the stations
options.B: It is exercised before the transactions take place at the stations
options.C: It is exercised by the statutory audit party after one year
options.D: It is exercised only after the close of the financial year

e: Traffic Accounts check is a post-check because it is exercised after the transactions have taken place and the accounts have been rendered by the stations.

q:
Consider the following statements about apportionment of coaching earnings:
1. Coaching earnings of through traffic are apportioned among the railways in proportion to the distance travelled over each railway.
2. Terminal charges are set apart before apportioning the coaching earnings of through traffic.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Coaching earnings of through traffic are apportioned in proportion to the distance travelled over each railway; the setting apart of terminal charges is a goods apportionment feature, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: Under the door-step banking arrangement for station earnings, the cash collected at a station is dealt with in the manner that:

options.A: The Station Master carries the cash personally to the Reserve Bank of India
options.B: The cash is retained at the station till the end of the financial year
options.C: The station cash is collected from the station by the authorised bank and deposited directly into the Railways' bank account
options.D: The cash is deposited in the personal account of the station cashier

e: Under door-step banking, station cash is collected from the station by the authorised bank and deposited directly into the Railways' bank account.

q: A tout caught unauthorisedly procuring and supplying reserved tickets to passengers for gain is prosecuted for touting, which is punishable under:

options.A: Section 106 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.B: Section 137 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.C: Section 141 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.D: Section 143 of the Railways Act, 1989

e: Touting - unauthorised procurement and supply of reserved tickets for gain - is punishable under Section 143 of the Railways Act, 1989.

q: A person who enters the station premises unauthorisedly and refuses to leave when asked to do so by the station staff commits trespass, punishable under:

options.A: Section 137 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.B: Section 147 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.C: Section 100 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.D: Section 93 of the Railways Act, 1989

e: Trespass on railway premises and refusal to leave when asked is punishable under Section 147 of the Railways Act, 1989.

q: As distinguished from Section 124A, which covers untoward incidents, compensation for the death of, or injury to, a passenger in a train accident, such as a collision or derailment of a passenger train, is payable under:

options.A: Section 124 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.B: Section 106 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.C: Section 141 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.D: Section 100 of the Railways Act, 1989

e: Compensation for death or injury in a train accident such as collision or derailment is payable under Section 124, while Section 124A covers untoward incidents.

q: A cement company purchases general purpose wagons of its own and inducts them into service for its traffic. Under the General Purpose Wagon Investment Scheme (GPWIS) of the Railways, in such a case:

options.A: Wagons are procured by the end user on lease from a wagon leasing company
options.B: The Railways purchase all the wagons owned by the private party
options.C: The customer invests in (purchases) general purpose wagons which are inducted into service, and is granted a rebate in freight for traffic loaded in such wagons
options.D: Freight rates for all commodities are fixed by the wagon owner himself

e: Under GPWIS, the customer invests in general purpose wagons inducted into service and gets a rebate in freight for traffic loaded in such wagons.

q: A passenger at home wants to know the expected arrival time and the running position of his train. The National Train Enquiry System (NTES) primarily provides:

options.A: Reservation of passenger tickets against vacant accommodation
options.B: Real-time information about the running of trains for the travelling public
options.C: Compilation of the traffic accounts of stations
options.D: Booking of goods traffic at stations

e: NTES primarily provides real-time information on the running of trains, including expected arrival, for the travelling public; it is not a booking or accounts system.

q: A goods supervisor follows his rake on the system from the time it is formed and placed for loading till it is released after unloading at the other end. In the Freight Operations Information System, the module which handles this rake formation, placement, movement and release work is the:

options.A: Terminal Management System (TMS)
options.B: Rake Management System (RMS)
options.C: Parcel Management System (PMS)
options.D: Coaching Operations Information System (COIS)

e: In FOIS, the Rake Management System (RMS) handles rake formation, placement, movement and release from loading to unloading.

q: Dispatchers are able to watch the movement of a train on their screens without waiting for station-to-station reports, because the Real Time Train Information System (RTIS) fitted on locomotives provides:

options.A: Data for fixation of freight rates
options.B: Statements of ticket sales at stations
options.C: Statistics of fuel consumption of locomotives
options.D: Automatic real-time information on the location and movement of trains

e: RTIS fitted on locomotives provides automatic real-time information on train location and movement, enabling dispatchers to watch trains without station-to-station reports.

q: A costing officer is asked what use the Railways make of the traffic costing data compiled by them. Traffic costing data are used by the Railways mainly for:

options.A: Providing a cost basis for the fixation and revision of fares and freight rates and for judging the remunerativeness of services
options.B: Fixation of pay and allowances of commercial staff
options.C: Printing of the Goods Tariff and the Coaching Tariff
options.D: Allotment of wagons to stations

e: Traffic costing data provide the cost basis for fixation and revision of fares and freight rates and for judging the remunerativeness of services.

q: A passenger who falls ill before his journey wants his reserved berth to be used by his son instead. Subject to the prescribed conditions, a passenger holding a reserved ticket may get the reservation transferred:

options.A: In favour of any person on payment of double the fare
options.B: Only in favour of a railway employee
options.C: In favour of a member of his family (blood relation)
options.D: In no case, as transfer of reservation is never permitted

e: Subject to prescribed conditions, a reserved ticket's reservation can be transferred in favour of a family member (blood relation), not to any person or only to a railway employee.

q: An operating officer works out the average gross load of the passenger trains of his railway for a period. The average gross load of passenger trains is computed as:

options.A: Gross Tonne Kilometres divided by route kilometres
options.B: Net Tonne Kilometres divided by passenger train kilometres
options.C: Gross Tonne Kilometres divided by passenger train kilometres
options.D: Passenger kilometres divided by train kilometres

e: Average gross load of passenger trains is Gross Tonne Kilometres divided by passenger train kilometres, i.e. the average gross tonnes hauled per train kilometre.
